facts.text: Van Nuys was founded in 1911 and named after rancher Isaac Newton Van Nuys, a Dutch‑ancestry entrepreneur.
The 1932 Art Deco Valley Municipal Building, now a Los Angeles Historic‑Cultural Monument, became the Valley’s first municipal civic center.
General Motors operated the Van Nuys Assembly plant from 1947 to 1992, producing cars on Van Nuys Boulevard and Arminta Street.
The former GM factory site now hosts The Plant shopping center, which opened in 1999 and includes a 16‑screen movie theater.
Van Nuys is the birthplace of Hollywood icons such as Natalie Wood, Robert Redford, Marilyn Monroe, and Jane Russell.
The Metro Orange Line’s Van Nuys station, opened in 2005, connects the neighborhood to downtown Los Angeles via the G Line.
